explain.say: First, the whole tree. It is an organism, which means one complete living thing. Now zoom to the leaf. A leaf is an organ, a body part made of different tissues working together. Can you name an organ in your own body?

faq.a: Yes. A leaf is made of several tissues, like the waxy skin, the palisade layer, the spongy layer and the veins, all working together to make food. That makes it an organ.
A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to do one job. Examples are palisade tissue in leaves, muscle tissue in your arm and xylem tissue that carries water in plants.
asks: Tell me about the palisade tissue

faq.a: An organelle is a small structure inside a cell with its own job, like the nucleus, a mitochondrion or a chloroplast.

faq.q: What are the levels of organisation?
faq.a: From small to big: organelle, cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism. Each level is made of many units of the level below.

faq.q: What is an organ system in a plant?
faq.a: In plants, the shoot system (stems, leaves and flowers) and the root system work as organ systems. In animals, examples are the digestive and circulatory systems.

facts: Palisade mesophyll cells sit just under the upper surface of a leaf and contain the most chloroplasts.
The levels of organisation are organelle, cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism.
